34. PREGNANCY & SPINAL CORD INJURY:

Maternal Risk:

UTI.

Epilepsy 20%.

DM (Obesity).

HTN

Latex allergy

Fetal Risks:

1 parent affected = 1 in 25 risks.

2 parents are affected = 1 in 7.

 

Lesions Above T4:

  • •Complete or partial

paralysis of respiratory

muscles.

  • •Difficultly initiation

in B.F

(Visual stimulation /

I/V oxytocin).

Lesions Above T6:

  • •Low baseline B.P.
  • •Low HR.
  • •Risk of Autonomic

Dysreflexia: AD

(emergency situation).

  • •Abnormal

thermoregulation.

  • →No reactive shivering,

sweating.

  • →Inadequate response

to environmental

temp change.

  • →Inflammation => febrile
  • →Response is

Inadequate

Above T10:

  • •Late pre – Term (15%)
  • •Unable to perceive labour pain.
  • •Unable to perceive FM.
  • •UTI.

Above T12:

malpresentation.

Above L2 L4:

- in adequate epidural Space.

  • •Breathing more difficult during pregnancy.
  • •Resp function by vital capacity.
  • •Physiotherapy, continuous positive airway pressure CPAP, Mechanical ventilation.

Vital capacity <12 – 15ml/kg => mechanical ventilation.

  • •Noxious stimuli => AD:

Triggers

  • -Urinary: distention, calculi, blocked catheter, UTI.
  • -GI: Haemorrhoids, constipation, appendicitis,
  • -Skin: tight clothing, Blister, burns, ulcers.
  • -R.S: periods, intercourse.
  • -Others: DVT.

S/S:

Rise in B.P 20 – 40 diagnostic

  • ⇨Nausea, vomiting, malaise, prickling sensation, thrombin headache, ringing in head.
  • ⇨Sweating, blushing, piloerection, tremors, nasal congestion, increased spasm.
  • ⇨Bradycardia, prolong PR internal AV Block disappearance of P WAVE, ventricular ECTOPIC BEATS.
  • ⇨Fetal bradycardia.

Treatment:

  • •Nifedipine S/L 10 – 40mg (1st line)

(S/L or bite & swallow tablets).

  • •GTN patch/spray.
  • •Nitroglycerine.
  • •Labetalol
  • •Hydralazine
  • •Avoidance of triggers

  • •Hospital admission @ 36 + 6 weeks:
  • -CTG.
  • -U.C palpations every 4 hours.
  • •Manual perception of contraction.
  • •Bladder emptying and A/B for asymptomatic bacteriuria,

ECV

 

 

 

 

 

 

Pre – conception discussion:

MDT:

Midwife, GP, Obstetric unit for delivery.

Anesthetist review.

Care, Support, social services.

 

SCi & Disability:

Understanding of condition.

Nature and limitation of disability.

Age & extent of spinal and pelvic injury.

Review medication.

Effect of Pregnancy:

Worsening immobility.

Worsening respiration.

Change of bladder care (need for catheter).

Delivery:

Early admission -> NVD planned.

 

Post-natal:

Information regarding websites.

Adaptive equipment

 

Table 34. Antenatal Problems in SCI:

system

Clinical Features

Management

Respiratory

system

* Breathing.

* Ability to cough.

* Bronchial secretions.

* Ventricular Perfusion miss match.

* Attacks of pneumonia.

- Physiotherapy.

- CPAP.

- Mechanical Ventilation.

CVS

* Bradycardia 40 – 45

* Hypotension 80/50/

- Baseline recording of B.P & HR @ Booking & @ every AN visit.

Genitourinary

* Risk of calculi:

  • -Urease producing bacterial infections.
  • -Immobilization.

* Risk of UTI:

  • -Long term catheter.
  • - Stasis and incontinence.

* Distended Bladder => trigger AD.

- Intermittent catheterization/ indwelling catheter/ Suprapubic.

- suprapubic catheter => change before 24 hours of C/S.

- keep bladder empty.

Bowels

* Constipation

* Can trigger AD

- Fiber.

- Timed bowel movements.

- Laxative.

- Gastro colic reflex utilization.

- Digital evacuation.

Skin

* Ulcers 6%.

* Atrophy.

- Skin Care.

- Pressure reliving mattress.

- Position change every 2 hours.

Bone

* Osteoporosis

Endocrine

* Risk of DM – 2.

Hematology

* Normocytic, normochromic anemia.

Thrombosis

* High risk in Acute SCI.

- score 1 for prophylaxis.

Psychological

* mood disorders.

Neurological

* Inability to respond appropriately

To acute illness.

Neuromuscular

* Spasticity.

* UMN – lesion.

* Below injury.

* 12% worsening in pregnancy.

- Baclofen (intrathecal).

- Oxybutynin.

- Diazepam.

 

 

 

IPC:

Uterine contractions travel via franken Hauser’s plexus @ T10.

Cervical dilatation perceives @ T11 T12.

Epidural – early especially in higher lesion to reduce AD.

Indwelling Cather.

Vaginal exam + catheterization => Gently + local Anaesthetic gel.

CEFM.

Avoid force flexion.

Instrumental delivery if AD is not controlled.

OVD with standard analgesia consider Rapid Spinal Anaesthesia.

Ergometrine can be given in women with no risk of AD

C/S:

47% if SCI @ T5.

20% if below T5.

On obstetric indication.

Skin incision 2cm above suprapubic catheter.

Suprapubic catheter.

Change catheter 24 hours before surgery.

Use of non-absorbable sutures on rectus & skin – remove 10th Day.

Physiotherapy to prevent DVT.

2 hourly care to prevent skin ulcers.

Episiotomy

Under standard anaesthesia – although pain not perceived but can trigger AD, so must give Anaesthesia => Absorbable structure.

 

Post op care => same as in normal Pts.

 

 

 

Contraception:

Pop, progesterone injection, implants = can be given

Male/ Female sterilization = can be offered

IUD, COC = Avoid.

SCI During Pregnancy:

Miscarriages & anomalies due to hypoxia in 1st .

Resuscitation & impatient AN care.

Thromboprophylaxis for 3m­0.
